title: Theophilus named compound colors with explicit nonnearest recipe reference and layer roles
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. Complete contiguous Theophilus I.1–9 defines named compound paints and explicitly resumes posc after intervening mixtures. Added ingredients and earlier/later paint layers constrain the reused reference; recipe identity, physical portion and deposited layer remain distinct. No Voynich writer or gloss.

design.scope_limit: One source mechanism and a complete connected historical section only. No target hypothesis, fixed test, decoder, reserve, new manuscript admission, refresh or commit.

full_source_inventory.coverage: Complete Latin of chapters I–IX, every ingredient/qualification/carrier/application/reference and source uncertainty; no omitted intervening chapter.

source.author: Theophilus Presbyter
source.date: Early twelfth-century work; early medieval witnesses conventionally dated approximately 1130. Exact bounded wording follows Hendrie1847 rather than a newly collated medieval folio.
source.native_status: All four relevant printed pages viewed natively and collated with the university HTML; three medieval witness-page images also viewed, but they show the prologue/later chapters rather than I–IX. No direct medieval I–IX diplomatic collation claimed.
source.image_relation: Instructions specify painted faces, eyes, hands, feet and detailed application regions. No complete surviving painting is claimed as this section's owned drawn endpoint.

attested_writing_mechanism: Introduce a named preparation by actually describing its ingredients and making it: membrina, posc, rosa, lumina and veneda.
Resume a specified earlier preparation by name and explicit backward wording: posc, de quo supra dictum est. It is not the last introduced mixture.
Use simple membrina after derived mixtures, then add stated ingredients to define further named colors.

Use a named color in different argument roles: cum rosa as input paint and super rosam as an applied color layer. The form difference is ordinary source-language case, not an invented target encoding.
Refer to earlier material/application states with anterior, anterioris coloris and super priorem, while preserving their local interpretive limits.

coupled_content.whole_claim: Membrina is defined and applied; prasinum, red from ochre and a little cenobrium make posc; the explicitly resumed posc receives additional prasinum/red to become a shadow of the earlier color.
coupled_content.consequence: The modified preparation inherits the earlier recipe rather than beginning from the immediately preceding veneda. Its exact amounts and initial complexion variant remain unspecified.

coupled_content.whole_claim: Simple membrina with cenobrium/minium makes rosa; later cenobrium is mixed with rosa and applied over prior rosa, leaving earlier color visible above and below.
coupled_content.consequence: Both recipe lineage and an earlier/later layer relation must be represented. The input paint and deposited layer are related but not one physical portion.

coupled_content.whole_claim: Simple membrina with ground cerosa makes lumina; only if the dark face needs more highlighting is additional white added and fine strokes placed over the earlier highlight.
coupled_content.consequence: A mandatory unconditional second stage would erase a written condition; a latest-mixture rule would resume rosa instead of the named highlight family.

coupled_content.whole_claim: Prasinus has its own water/straining preparation and fresh-wall use. Veneda is made from black/little white, increased with white for eye regions, separated by plain white and washed with water.
coupled_content.consequence: These intervening chapters remain present. They cannot be silently deleted to make every relevant reference local.

distinct_rivals.rival: Always reuse the latest named mixture.
distinct_rivals.different_consequence: I.7 takes veneda where the source explicitly names posc; I.4/I.5 also fail to return to simple membrina.

distinct_rivals.rival: Each color mention is a new primitive material with independent composition.
distinct_rivals.different_consequence: It drops inherited base ingredients and stated additions, even if a plausible final shade can be assigned.

distinct_rivals.rival: The later rose application simply replaces the entire earlier layer.
distinct_rivals.different_consequence: It cannot preserve the earlier color visible above and below as required in I.8.

distinct_rivals.rival: Every reference must repeat the complete earlier written name unchanged.
distinct_rivals.different_consequence: Actual rosa/rosam case variation and compressed local references contradict a universal literal-recurrence rule in this source; no old target model is thereby rescued.

design.no_modern_program_language: The proposal owns the historical named-definition/backreference construction itself. It supplies no synthetic opcode alphabet, arbitrary per-word dictionary, parser-generated carrier defaults, fixed source-count serializer or free modern program grammar.
source_debts_and_symmetries: The source does not decide whether an earlier mixture is saved stock or freshly made equivalent recipe. Type continuity is not individual-portion identity or mass conservation.
Amounts are mostly qualitative and I.1 explicitly permits discretionary complexion-dependent mixtures; no numeric ratio or unique spectral prediction follows.
Prasinus is described and processed but its full chemical composition is not given.
No general oil, egg or glue binder is written in I–IX; water has only the locally specified roles.
Some pronoun and predecessor-layer scopes require contextual interpretation; they are not all as explicit as posc, de quo supra dictum est.
A simultaneous renaming of all material families preserves much of the dependency structure; no literal human-language names are identified by structure alone.
The whole source section and its actual source-language inflection do not supply a finite target writing contract. No EVA=Latin or suffix assignment is assumed.
The relevant medieval chapter pages were not directly collated; native print/HTML conflicts are preserved, and pre-1450 work identity is distinct from exact1847edition wording.
